chunks: That was narrated by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Yazid al-Kunasī, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who pronounced dhihar from his wife, then divorced her with a single divorce. He said: 'If he divorces her with a single divorce, the dhihar becomes void, and the divorce demolishes the dhihar.'
He said, so I said to him: 'Does he have the right to take her back?' He said: 'Yes, she is his wife.'
He said: 'If he takes her back, it becomes obligatory upon him what is obligatory upon the one who pronounced dhihar, before they touch each other.'

I said: 'If he leaves her until her waiting period (iddah) expires and she gains full control of herself, then he marries her afterwards, does the dhihar remain obligatory upon him before he touches her?' He said: 'No, she has become completely divorced from him and she has gained control of herself.'

I said: 'If he pronounced dhihar from her and did not touch her, and left her, not touching her except that he sees her while she is undressed (without clothing), without touching her, does anything remain obligatory upon him?' He said: 'She is his wife, and her intercourse is not forbidden to him, but what is obligatory upon the one who pronounced dhihar before he has intercourse with her is obligatory upon him, and she is his wife.'

I said: 'If she raises him to the ruler (judge) and says: 'This is my husband, he has pronounced dhihar from me, and he has kept me from touching me, fearing that what is obligatory upon the one who pronounced dhihar will become obligatory upon him,' he said: 'It is not obligatory upon him to be compelled to free a slave, fast, and feed, if he does not have what to free, is not able to fast, and does not find what to give in charity.'
And he said: 'If he is able to free a slave, then it is upon the Imam to compel him to free a slave and give charity, before he touches her and after he touches her.'

key_terms.الإِطْعَامُ: Feeding (the tertiary expiation if one cannot fast).
key_terms.الإِمَامُ: The Imam (or judge) who compels the performance of the expiation.
key_terms.الصِّيَامُ: Fasting (the secondary expiation if one cannot free a slave).
key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Dhihar: A form of divorce in Islamic law where a husband declares his wife's back like his mother's back, prohibiting intercourse until expiation is made.
key_terms.العِتْقُ: Freeing a slave (the primary expiation for dhihar).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dhihar if a man divorces his wife and then takes her back?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a single divorce (*talaq*) abrogates the *dhihar* status, yet the husband remains liable for the expiation if he remarries her before consummation. It further distinguishes between voluntary delay and forced compliance, noting that the Imam compels the expiation only if the husband has the means, reflecting the Shia principle of graded financial capacity in *kaffarah*.
